- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use 3-day moving average to dampen.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% to prevent overbought bias.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 5–10 day moving average or 30-day trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply linear decay or exponential smoothing to reduce initial bias.
- If sentiment is flat or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often drifts toward historical mean; anchor forecast to 30-day rolling average or use sentiment-weighted median.
